key_insight: Leveraging generative modeling in pixel space enables a monocular depth foundation model (Pixel-Perfect Depth, PPD) to produce high-quality, flying-pixel-free point clouds that preserve fine geometric details.
problem_solved: Existing geometry foundation models produce noisy point clouds with ‘flying pixels’ and lose fine details; this work eliminates those artifacts while recovering cleaner, more accurate geometry from images.
method: Introduce Pixel-Perfect Depth (PPD): a monocular depth foundation model that uses pixel-space generative priors to predict extremely accurate per-pixel depth.
Convert pixel-perfect depth maps into point clouds with explicit suppression of flying-pixel outliers and mechanisms to retain fine geometric details.
Train and evaluate at scale to demonstrate consistent improvements in depth accuracy and artifact reduction compared to prior geometry models.
impact: Provides practitioners with a practical way to obtain clean, high-fidelity 3D geometry from monocular images, improving downstream tasks in robotics, AR, and 3D reconstruction by reducing artifacts and preserving detail.
visual_elements: Before vs. after point-cloud comparison highlighting flying-pixel removal and finer detail recovery
Architecture diagram of PPD showing image → pixel-space generative module → depth map → point cloud pipeline
Quantitative bar/line charts: depth error, flying-pixel rate, and detail-preservation metrics vs. baselines
Application thumbnails: AR overlay and robotic perception scenes demonstrating practical improvements
paper_authors: Gangwei Xu, Haotong Lin, Hongcheng Luo, Haiyang Sun, Bing Wang
